original_question: A square-free monomial ideal I ⊆ S = K[x0, ..., xn] is called a square-free Gotzmann ideal when it can be written as m1(x_i : i in J1) + m1m2(x_i : i in J2) + ... + m1...ms(x_i : i in Js) for square-free monomials m1, ..., ms and pairwise disjoint subsets J1, ..., Js of {0, 1, ..., n}. Which square-free Gotzmann ideals satisfy the weak Lefschetz property, and do any Artinian reductions of Stanley-Reisner ideals of chordal complexes satisfy the weak Lefschetz property?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper: it uses the same ambient ring S = K[x_0, ..., x_n], the same Hoefel-Mermin normal-form description of square-free Gotzmann ideals, and it reproduces the same two-part open question about WLP for square free Gotzmann ideals and for Artinian reductions of Stanley-Reisner ideals of chordal complexes. ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: Section 2 works under the standing assumption that the base field K has characteristic 0 unless explicitly stated otherwise; your draft omits that hypothesis. ([uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl](https://uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2-1.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The paper asks about the weak Lefschetz property in a section devoted to Artinian graded algebras, so a stand-alone version should make explicit that WLP is being asked for the associated standard graded Artinian quotient (in the first clause, this means at least restricting to the Artinian case S/I). ([uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl](https://uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2-1.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To be fully self-contained, the standard definition of WLP should be stated explicitly: there exists a linear form ell such that multiplication by ell from degree d to degree d+1 has maximal rank for every d. The paper uses the abbreviation 'WLP' without restating this definition in Question 2.13 itself. ([uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl](https://uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2-1.pdf?utm_source=openai))

For the second clause, the paper's exact wording is 'Do (some) Artinian reductions of Stanley-Reisner ideals of chordal complexes satisfy the WLP?'; your draft's 'do any' is close, but the official formulation is slightly softer. ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The meaning of 'Artinian reduction' is left implicit in the paper; to make the question stand-alone, it helps to say that one is quotienting by a linear system of parameters. ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The standard grading on S is implicit in the paper's setup and should be stated if the question is to stand alone. ([uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl](https://uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2-1.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Over a field K of characteristic 0, let S = K[x_0, ..., x_n] with its standard grading, and let I subseteq S be a square-free Gotzmann ideal, i.e. an ideal of the form I = m_1(x_i : i in J_1) + m_1m_2(x_i : i in J_2) + ... + m_1...m_s(x_i : i in J_s), where m_1, ..., m_s are square-free monomials and J_1, ..., J_s are pairwise disjoint subsets of {0, 1, ..., n}. Among those I for which S/I is Artinian, determine which quotients S/I have the weak Lefschetz property, meaning that there exists a linear form ell in (S/I)_1 such that multiplication by ell from (S/I)_d to (S/I)_{d+1} has maximal rank for every d; and, relatedly, determine whether there exist chordal complexes Delta whose Stanley-Reisner ideals I_Delta admit Artinian reductions S/(I_Delta + (ell_1, ..., ell_r)) by a linear system of parameters that have the weak Lefschetz property. ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft clearly targets Question 2.13, not Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3, because the only place where the paper discusses square free Gotzmann ideals in the Hoefel-Mermin form and connects them to Stanley-Reisner ideals of chordal complexes is the Gotzmann-ideals paragraph immediately preceding Question 2.13. The only paper-faithful sharpening needed is to make explicit the section-wide characteristic-0 hypothesis and the Artinian/WLP conventions that the paper leaves implicit in this short problem list. The paper does not supply an equivalent reformulation of Question 2.13, so no alternate formulation should be added. ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))
